briefdescription.para: Encode a document as a hierarchical TT (HTTrain).

detaileddescription.para:
The document is split into segments (paragraphs or sentences depending on hint). Each segment is encoded as a fixed-length embedding vector. The encoding tier is selected by priority:
Registered ITextEncoder (if isAvailable())
Injected EmbedFn bridge (STUB #257)
Built-in lexical encoder (unigram + bigram + char-trigram features, L2-normalised) — degraded mode, EncoderQuality::LEXICAL
The resulting segment × embed_dim matrix is decomposed via HT-SVD into an HTTrain.

briefdescription.para: Converts heterogeneous data sources into tensor-native (TT/HT) formats.

detaileddescription.para: All methods are static and stateless. Thread-safe.
UTRConverter exposes two injectable bridges so that real encoder backends can replace the built-in fallback implementations without changing callers:

listitem.para: EmbedFn (setEmbedFn) — replaces the built-in lexical embedding used in fromDocument(). The callable receives (segment, embed_dim) and must return a std::vector<float> of exactly embed_dim elements.

ImageEmbedFn (setImageEmbedFn) — replaces the raw-pixel TT encoding in fromImage(). The callable receives the flat HWC pixel buffer and the three dimensions plus the UTR config, and must return a valid TTTrain.

detaileddescription.para: Both bridges are stored in static std::mutex-guarded slots. Call clearEmbedFn() / clearImageEmbedFn() to revert to the built-in fallback. The fallback is retained when no bridge is set (fail-open for encode quality, not for correctness — structural invariants are always maintained).

para.heading: Encoder Object APIs (preferred over raw bridge functions)

detaileddescription.para: Higher-level plugins should implement ITextEncoder / IImageEncoder and register them via setTextEncoder() / setImageEncoder(). These encoder objects take priority over the raw EmbedFn / ImageEmbedFn bridges. If isAvailable() returns false on the registered encoder, the system falls back to the bridge function tier (if any), then to the built-in lexical/patch encoder.
